cards.front: Recall a key point about Materials and Manufacturing
cards.back: Material categories: woods (hardwood, softwood, manufactured), metals (ferrous, non-ferrous), polymers (thermoplastic, thermoset), ceramics.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Materials and Manufacturing
cards.back: Manufacturing processes: subtractive (CNC, laser cutting), additive (3D printing), forming (vacuum forming, injection moulding).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Materials and Manufacturing
cards.back: Material properties determine suitability: strength, weight, flexibility, durability, cost, sustainability and aesthetic qualities.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Materials and Manufacturing
cards.back: Joining methods: permanent (welding, adhesive, rivets) and temporary (screws, bolts, nuts) — choose based on function and disassembly needs.

cards.front: What should you know about three-dimensional design exam tips?
cards.back: Always justify material choices with SPECIFIC PROPERTIES. Know the difference between thermoplastic and thermoset. Understand which manufacturing process suits which quantity (one-off vs batch vs mass). Consider sustainability in material selection.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: 3D printing can replace all other manufacturing methods. Correct: 3D printing is excellent for prototyping and complex geometries, but has limitations: slow for mass production, limited material range, and weaker structural properties than moulded or machined parts. Each manufacturing method has strengths — choose the RIGHT process for the task.
Select a product and analyse its material and manufacturing choices. Explain why each material was chosen and suggest more sustainable alternatives where possible.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Materials and Manufacturing
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Materials and Manufacturing using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.
